honorific: Forms of address, register and fidelity guidance (zh→en): translate dialogue and narration into natural, punchy English suited to Chinese serial storytelling (xianxia, wuxia, urban/system, historical/court). Render cultivation, martial, sect and seniority titles consistently by relationship and setting (e.g., 师兄/师姐 as Senior Brother/Senior Sister, 师父 as Master, 前辈 as Senior, 道友 as Fellow Daoist, 宗主 as Sect Master, 长老 as Elder) and keep system/status prompts (【...】 / [...]) crisp and game-like. Render imperial, noble and humble self-references naturally by speaker role (e.g., 孤/朕/寡人 as 'I' or majestic 'we', never 'the lone one'; 臣 as 'Your servant'/'Your subject'; 大人/殿下/公子/先生 graded by hierarchy, never ungrammatical calques like 'the sir'). Avoid stiff Chinese calques: drop demonstrative 'That' before a named character (那<Name> -> '<Name>'), never insert unrequested parenthetical glosses or translator notes into prose, and match singular vs. plural to the characters present. Preserve source logic faithfully across multi-clause sentences—negation scope, conditionals, exact numbers, agent/object direction and kinship seniority. Translate idioms (成语) by contextual meaning rather than surface words, and format embedded poems, chants or lyrics with explicit line breaks (\n).
